userPrompt: Does the GDPR let me keep customer data forever if I got consent once?
responseText:
**No.**

GDPR does **not** let you keep customer data forever just because you obtained consent once.

### Key limitations
- **Consent must be informed and specific.** The data subject must know the purposes and how long you intend to keep the data (Art. 13/14). Vague “forever” consent is almost always invalid.
- **Consent can be withdrawn at any time** (Art. 7(3)). When withdrawn, you must stop processing and, in most cases, delete the data unless another lawful basis or legal obligation applies.
- **Storage limitation principle** (Art. 5(1)(e)): You must delete or anonymise personal data when it is no longer necessary for the purpose(s) for which it was collected. “Forever” almost never satisfies this.
- Even with valid initial consent, you must periodically review whether continued storage is still justified. Perpetual retention based on one-time consent is unlawful in practice.

### Practical reality in the EU
Regulators (and courts) treat indefinite retention on the basis of one-time consent as a violation. You need either:
- a clear, limited retention period that you actually enforce, or
- another lawful basis (e.g. legal obligation, legitimate interest with a proper balancing test and deletion policy).

**Bottom line:** One-time consent does not create a perpetual GDPR-compliant right to keep customer data. You must delete it when it is no longer necessary or when the data subject objects/withdraws consent and no other basis applies.
